epic.title: Substrate: DNS and VPN first, 30 days untouched before June
epic.description:
Substrate is a separate, silent, always-on box built from spare parts beside the routers, for cutting monthly costs, privacy and owning the data, not depending on companies, and the enjoyment of learning (not to cancel anything). Nothing is exposed to the internet: VPN only. House basics fail safe, Kirsty never notices it, anything she uses changes only in one weekend window with a rehearsed revert, and backups go to a second drive and an encrypted drive at a family member's house.

## Order
First the costed list and power measurement (sub.01) and the platform choice (sub.02), then the build and power-cut test (sub.03), the first service by hand then as code (sub.04) and the names and certificates (sub.05). Network needs come next: the DNS filter where net.03 decided (sub.06) and the VPN on net.04's route with Kirsty's phone (sub.07). Then Home Assistant (sub.08), monitoring (sub.09, sub.21), cameras (sub.10), backups (sub.11), photos (sub.12), files (sub.13), media, books and feeds (sub.14), paperwork (sub.15), git and runners (sub.16) and the PC worker question (sub.17). Alongside: the off test (sub.18), Kirsty's phone weeks (sub.19), the family rule (sub.20), monthly updates (sub.22), restore tests (sub.23) and the printed page (sub.24). The 30-day proof runs hands off from 2027-04-24 and is checked 2027-05-24 (sub.25); the done check (sub.26) closes the epic. H2.3 (a better home than IONOS) is keys.14 and the old VPS check is keys.08, both in E.keys and linked here.

## Done means
Every chosen service runs 30 days without Phil touching it, Kirsty's services have each worked a week untouched on her phone, and the printed page is by the routers.

## Flags
No [claude] flags touch this epic. The old VPS items (H2.5, assumed) are checked in keys.08; nothing is switched off without Phil's word.

## Dossier
The research dossier is attached in Docs (link added by the integrator).

tickets.title: Costed list: the spare parts as a whole machine, silence, a plug-in meter's week of power, monthly running figure; budget decided after
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code writes the costed list for Substrate in Docs: every spare part Phil has (CPU and whether it has integrated graphics, board, RAM, drives, PSU and its wattage, case, fans, any graphics card), what is missing to make a whole machine, and a priced line for each missing part (to be priced, nothing bought). It adds the silence plan (large fans on a slow BIOS curve, a PSU whose fan stays off at light load, SSD for the system, any hard drive spinning down) and an estimated idle draw. Phil's part is two short sittings: list the parts (photos of the labels are fine) and, once a plug-in meter is in the house, leave the bench-assembled machine on it for a week. The monthly figure uses about 24p per watt per month (Ofgem cap 32.69p per kWh from 1 January 2027; Phil's own tariff replaces it if known). The list states the figure with and without any graphics card.

## Why
Phil: "decide after a costed list"; "measure first with a plug-in meter for a week, then set a limit"; noise "silent or near it" shapes which parts are used.

## Done looks like
A Docs page with the parts table, the missing parts priced, the measured or estimated idle watts, a monthly and yearly running figure, and one line for Phil: the budget he sets and the power limit.

## Unlocks
sub.03 (the build uses this list); sub.10 (the camera plan depends on whether the CPU has integrated graphics); sub.17 (the graphics card question).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Cost
Parts, drives and a plug-in meter are to be priced on the list. Nothing is bought in this run.

tickets.title: Platform research: plain Linux with containers against a VM host (the VM question folded in); Phil approves
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code writes a one-page comparison in Docs of two shapes for Substrate: plain Debian with Docker Compose (Home Assistant as a container, no add-ons, filesystem snapshots and pinned versions for revert), and Proxmox VE 9.2 with a Home Assistant OS VM plus one Debian VM running Docker Compose (per-VM snapshots and backups). It scores them on: the family rule's snapshot and one-step revert, Home Assistant add-ons and updates, camera detection on the integrated graphics, idle power and RAM on the spare parts, upkeep in evenings, and learning. The H5 "VM question" is answered here. Phil reads it and writes his choice on the ticket.

## Why
Phil: "research, then he approves" (plain Linux with containers versus a VM host); H5 folded the VM question into this research.

## Done looks like
The Docs page exists and the ticket carries Phil's choice in one line (for example "Proxmox, two VMs" or "Debian and Compose").

## Unlocks
sub.03 (what gets installed); sub.08 (the Home Assistant install method); sub.20 (how the snapshot and revert work).

## Depends on
Nothing.

tickets.title: Build the box beside the routers; power-cut restart tested by pulling the plug
tickets.description:
## What
Build Substrate from the sub.01 parts, place it beside the routers on a wired connection, set the BIOS to power on after a power cut and to a quiet fan curve, install the platform Phil chose in sub.02, then pull the plug once and confirm it starts by itself.

## Why
Phil: a separate always-on box "beside the routers"; power cut: "restart cleanly by itself; tested by pulling the plug once".

## Done looks like
Substrate sits beside the routers, near silent, on a fixed house address, and the pulled-plug test is ticked with "started by itself: yes".

## Unlocks
sub.04 (services as code); sub.05 (names and certificates).

## Depends on
sub.01 (the parts and budget); sub.02 (which platform).

steps_definition.title: Build Substrate and test the power-cut restart

intro.answer: Build the box, set the BIOS to power on after a power cut, install the platform, pull the plug once.

sources.label: ASUS, BIOS item Restore AC Power Loss

hard_part.why: The installer wipes the system SSD; check it is the right drive.

phases.title: Build the box
needs: The parts on the costed list

steps.title: Assemble the machine
steps.body_html: Build the machine from the parts on the sub.01 list. Fit the system SSD. Leave any graphics card out unless sub.01 says it stays.
steps.expect_html: All parts fitted, case closed, fans connected to the board's fan headers.

steps.title: Place it beside the routers
steps.body_html: Put Substrate in a ventilated spot beside the routers. Connect one Ethernet cable from the RT-AX86U's LAN port to the box. Plug the power into the wall, not a switched extension.
steps.expect_html: Box in place, cable in a LAN port, link light on.

phases.title: BIOS settings
needs: Keyboard and screen plugged into the box

steps.title: Power on after a power cut

where.label: BIOS: Advanced or Power Management, "Restore on AC Power Loss"

steps.body_html: Set Restore on AC Power Loss (also called AC Power Recovery or After Power Loss) to Power On.

troubleshooting.fix: Look under Chipset or APM; on some boards it is under Advanced, APM Configuration. Write the board model on the ticket and Claude finds it.

steps.title: Quiet fan curve and power saving

where.label: BIOS: fan control and CPU power settings

steps.body_html: Set the case and CPU fans to a quiet or silent curve. Turn on C-states and ASPM if the BIOS offers them. Save and exit.
steps.expect_html: The box is near silent at idle.

steps.title: Record the board
steps.body_html: Note the board model and BIOS version.

phases.title: Install the platform chosen in sub.02

steps.title: Write the installer
steps.body_html: Claude Code downloads the installer for the platform Phil chose (Proxmox VE 9.2 or Debian 13) and writes it to the USB stick, checking the checksum.
steps.expect_html: A bootable stick and a matching checksum.

steps.title: Install

where.label: Substrate, booted from the USB stick

steps.body_html: Boot from the stick and install to the system SSD with the defaults Claude's note gives (host name substrate, a fixed house address agreed in E.net). Save the root or admin password in Proton Pass.
steps.expect_html: Substrate reboots and shows its login prompt with its address.

notes.html: Save the password in Proton Pass only. Never paste it into a chat, a ticket or the config repo.

phases.title: Pull the plug once
needs: Five minutes when nobody needs the internet

steps.title: Pull the plug
steps.body_html: With Substrate running, switch off at the wall or pull the plug. Wait 30 seconds.

steps.title: Plug back in and wait
steps.body_html: Plug it back in. Do not press the power button.
steps.expect_html: Substrate starts by itself and reaches its login prompt within about five minutes.

troubleshooting.fix: Check step 2.1 again; ASUS advises leaving the PSU off about 30 seconds before testing.

tickets.title: The first service by hand with a guide, then everything as code: the config repo and a runbook per service in Docs
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code writes a short guide and Phil builds the first service by hand on Substrate: Uptime Kuma, the status checker, chosen because a mistake there breaks nothing Kirsty uses. Then Claude Code creates the private config repo (Compose files or VM definitions, pinned versions, no secret values; secrets in a separate file on Substrate only), rebuilds the same service from the repo to prove it, and writes the runbook template in Docs (what it is, where it lives, how to update, how to revert, how to restore, who uses it). Every later service gets a runbook from the template.

## Why
Phil: "build the first service by hand with a guide, then everything as code"; docs are "config in a git repo plus a runbook per service in Docs".

## Done looks like
Uptime Kuma runs from the repo; the repo has no secret values; the runbook template and Uptime Kuma's runbook are in Docs.

## Unlocks
sub.06, sub.07, sub.11, sub.16, sub.22 (every service and the update routine build on the repo).

## Depends on
sub.03 (the box and platform).

tickets.title: Names under sporebit.com with real certificates, resolving only inside the house or over the VPN
tickets.description:
## What
Give Substrate's services names under sporebit.com with a real wildcard certificate from Let's Encrypt, issued by the DNS-01 challenge through the IONOS DNS API (sporebit.com's DNS is at IONOS). No public A record is created; the names resolve only through the house DNS filter or over the VPN. A wildcard keeps service names out of the public certificate logs. Phil creates the IONOS API key and keeps it in Proton Pass; Claude Code configures the proxy.

## Why
Phil: "names under sporebit.com with real certificates, resolving only inside the house or over the VPN".

## Done looks like
status.(pattern) opens with a padlock at home; it does not resolve on mobile data; the certificate renews by itself; the IONOS key is in Proton Pass and named in the E.keys inventory.

## Unlocks
sub.06 onwards (every service gets a name); sub.21 (the status page address).

## Depends on
sub.03 (the box). The inside-only answer needs sub.06's local names; until then the proxy is checked by address.

intro.answer: A wildcard certificate by DNS-01 at IONOS, names that resolve only at home.

sources.label: IONOS help, API key prefix and secret

hard_part.why: The key's reach decides how much damage a leaked key could do.

phases.title: Choose the names and the key's reach

steps.title: Pick the name pattern
steps.body_html: Choose between service names directly under sporebit.com (for example photos.sporebit.com) or under a house subdomain (photos.home.sporebit.com). The house subdomain keeps them apart from public sites.

steps.title: Pick the key's reach
steps.body_html: The IONOS DNS API key can change DNS records in the account. Choose: A one IONOS key used directly, or B a CNAME from _acme-challenge to a small separate zone, so the key only ever touches that zone. B is safer and takes Claude Code about 30 minutes more.
steps.expect_html: A or B written in the field.

notes.html: Cloudflare is not used here: its free plan needs the whole sporebit.com zone moved, mail records included.

phases.title: Make the key and the certificate

steps.title: Create the IONOS DNS API key
steps.body_html: Create a new API key named substrate-acme. Copy the prefix and the secret into a new Proton Pass item called IONOS DNS API key (Substrate).
steps.expect_html: The key is listed in IONOS and saved in Proton Pass.

notes.html: Save the password in Proton Pass only. Never paste it into a chat, a ticket or the config repo.

steps.title: Put the key on Substrate

where.label: Substrate terminal, the secrets file Claude names

steps.body_html: Paste the key into the secrets file on Substrate that Claude Code's note names, by typing it there yourself. It never goes into the config repo or a chat.
steps.expect_html: The file exists and only root can read it.

notes.html: Add this key to the E.keys inventory (keys.01) by name.

steps.title: Issue the wildcard certificate
steps.body_html: Claude Code configures the reverse proxy for a wildcard certificate by the DNS-01 challenge at IONOS (lego's ionos provider or Caddy's ionos module) and adds the name for Uptime Kuma.
steps.expect_html: A Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate is issued and renews by itself.

phases.title: Check it resolves only at home

steps.title: Open the status name at home
steps.body_html: Open the Uptime Kuma name (for example status.home.sporebit.com).
steps.expect_html: The page opens with a padlock and no certificate warning.

steps.title: Check it is invisible outside

where.label: Phone on mobile data, VPN off

steps.body_html: Open the same name with Wi-Fi off and the VPN off.
steps.expect_html: The name does not resolve. Nothing at home is reachable.

tickets.title: Service: the DNS filter, wherever net.03 decided (Substrate, the router or hosted)
tickets.description:
## What
Run the house DNS filter on Substrate if net.03 chose Substrate (AdGuard Home or Pi-hole as net.03 says), from the config repo, with local names for every Substrate service, a fallback resolver agreed before the house is switched over, and the router's DHCP pointed at it in a weekend window.

## Why
Phil's order: "network needs first: DNS filter and VPN"; house basics fail safe: "internet and light switches work with the server off".

## Done looks like
Every device in the house uses the filter; the fallback is written down and works (proved in sub.18); the runbook is in Docs.

## Unlocks
sub.08 and sub.09 (they follow the filter); E.block's block.03 and block.04 (blocking on the filter); sub.25 (part of the 30-day proof).

## Depends on
net.03 (where the filter runs and which one); sub.04 (the config repo).

## Red team
- Finding 30: Moves epic if net.03's answer is not Substrate.

intro.answer: Install the filter, agree a fallback, test one device, then switch the house in a weekend window.

hard_part.why: Without a fallback the house loses the internet whenever Substrate is off.

phases.title: Install the filter and sign in

steps.title: Install the filter as code
steps.body_html: Claude Code adds the DNS filter net.03 chose (AdGuard Home or Pi-hole) to the config repo, with the upstream resolvers net.03 names, and starts it on Substrate.
steps.expect_html: The filter's page answers at its sporebit.com name.

steps.title: Set the admin login
steps.body_html: Create the admin login and save it in Proton Pass as Substrate DNS filter.
steps.expect_html: You are signed in to the dashboard.

notes.html: Save the password in Proton Pass only. Never paste it into a chat, a ticket or the config repo.

steps.title: Add the local names
steps.body_html: Claude Code adds the local DNS answers for every Substrate service name (DNS rewrites or local DNS records).
steps.expect_html: The status name resolves to Substrate's house address.

phases.title: Fallback, then one device by hand

steps.title: Agree the fallback
steps.body_html: Write down what answers DNS when Substrate is off: a second filter, the router, or nothing. Without a fallback, the whole house loses the internet when Substrate is off.
steps.expect_html: The fallback is written in the field.

fields.label: Fallback resolver
fields.placeholder: for example the RT-AX86U, or a second filter

steps.title: Test on the PC only

where.label: Windows network settings on the PC

steps.body_html: Set the PC's DNS by hand to Substrate's address. Browse for a few minutes, then open a test address from the blocking epic's list.
steps.expect_html: Ordinary sites load; the test address is blocked.

steps.title: Point the router's DHCP at Substrate

where.label: RT-AX86U: LAN, DHCP Server, DNS Server 1 and 2

steps.body_html: Set DNS Server 1 to Substrate's address and DNS Server 2 to the fallback from step 2.1. Apply.
steps.expect_html: The router shows the new DNS servers.

notes.html: Family service: change it only in the set weekend window, snapshot first, revert rehearsed (sub.20). Never on a weeknight.
Revert: clear both fields and Apply; devices go back to the router's own DNS on their next renewal or a Wi-Fi toggle.

steps.title: Check a phone and a TV
steps.body_html: Toggle Wi-Fi on your phone, browse, then start something on one TV.
steps.expect_html: Both work; the filter's dashboard shows their queries.

tickets.title: Service: the VPN; Kirsty's phone gets it
tickets.description:
## What
Make Substrate the VPN node on the route net.04 chose, so phones and laptops reach the house services and cameras from outside with nothing exposed to the internet. Phil's phone is tested on mobile data first, then Kirsty's phone gets the app.

## Why
Phil: exposure "nothing; VPN only. Kirsty's phone gets the VPN."

## Done looks like
From mobile data with the VPN on, the status page opens; with it off, nothing at home answers; Kirsty's phone shows connected.

## Unlocks
sub.19 (Kirsty's untouched week); sub.24 (the printed page); net.21 (the remote access guide); sub.25.

## Depends on
sub.04 (the config repo); net.04 (which VPN route).

steps_definition.title: The VPN on Substrate, and Kirsty's phone

intro.answer: Substrate becomes the VPN node; Phil's phone tested outside, then Kirsty's phone set up.

phases.title: Substrate as the VPN node, and Phil's phone

steps.title: Set up the VPN on Substrate
steps.body_html: Claude Code sets Substrate up as the route net.04 chose (for example a Tailscale subnet router advertising the house network, with the house DNS filter as the VPN's DNS, or a WireGuard server). No port is opened unless net.04 says so.
steps.expect_html: Substrate shows as connected in the VPN's admin page.

steps.title: Approve the route

steps.expect_html: Kirsty knows it is there. sub.19 then counts the untouched week.

tickets.title: Service: Home Assistant
tickets.description:
## What
Install Home Assistant on Substrate the way sub.02 chose, create the owner account, add the house's devices by room, put its backups in the backup set, and list what must keep working when it is off. The baby monitor is added for live view only, never recorded.

## Why
Phil: Home Assistant is part of the house services; it is the control route for the wall dashboard; house basics fail safe.

## Done looks like
Home Assistant opens at its sporebit.com name, every device has a room, a backup exists, and the must-work list is on the ticket for sub.18.

## Unlocks
sub.10 (cameras); sub.18 (the off test); E.wall's wall.17, E.home's home.24, E.baby's baby.12 (controls, scenes and the monitor); sub.25.

## Depends on
sub.06 (the DNS filter first, Phil's order); sub.02 fixes the install method.

steps.title: Install Home Assistant

steps.title: Create the owner account
steps.body_html: Create the owner account, set the home location, units (metric) and time zone (Europe/London). Save the login in Proton Pass as Home Assistant (Substrate).

tickets.title: Service: local camera recording, motion clips for a set number of days, doorbell and outdoor only
tickets.description:
## What
Record the doorbell and outdoor cameras locally on Substrate with Frigate, keeping motion clips for a number of days Phil sets. Detection runs on the CPU's integrated graphics where it has them (Frigate no longer recommends a Coral for new installs). The baby monitor is never recorded; it is live view through Home Assistant only. First check each camera offers a local stream.

## Why
Phil: "motion clips for a set number of days, doorbell and outdoor cameras only; the baby monitor is live view, never recorded"; cameras local only, no cloud.

## Done looks like
A walk past an outdoor camera gives a clip; clips older than the set days are gone; the baby monitor is not in Frigate.

## Unlocks
E.wall's doorbell pop-up on the shared-room screen; sub.18 (off test).

## Depends on
sub.08 (Home Assistant first); sub.01 (whether the CPU has integrated graphics).

intro.answer: Doorbell and outdoor cameras, motion clips for a set number of days, never the baby monitor.

tickets.title: Service: backups, second drive plus an encrypted off-site drive at a family member's house
tickets.description:
## What
Back Substrate up nightly to a second drive and periodically to an encrypted off-site drive kept at a family member's house, with restic or borg (both encrypt on the client). The set covers the config repo, each service's data with proper database dumps, and Home Assistant's backups. The backup password lives in Proton Pass and a sealed printed copy.

## Why
Phil: "second drive plus an encrypted off-site copy"; off-site "a drive at a family member's house"; worry: a data-loss scare.

## Done looks like
A nightly snapshot on the second drive, one complete off-site copy at the family member's house, the password in Proton Pass and on paper, and the refresh interval written down.

## Unlocks
sub.12, sub.13 (photos and files need backups first); sub.23 (restore tests).

## Depends on
sub.04 (the config repo); MYC-182 (Phil's answer about the backup drive).

## Cost
The second drive and the off-site drive are to be priced on sub.01 if not spare. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 28: Drives bought only from the approved costed list (sub.01); MYC-182 asks about the backup drive.
- Finding 67: The backup encryption key is in Proton Pass and on paper in a second place; a backup whose key is lost is not a backup.

tickets.title: Service: photo library with phone upload, run beside the phones' cloud for three months, then a tested restore and a decision

Run Immich on Substrate with upload from the phones, beside iCloud or Google Photos (nothing in the phones' cloud changes). Kirsty's phone follows through sub.19.

Phil: "run beside the phones' cloud photos first, decide after three months and a tested restore".

## Done looks like
Phil's photos upload; after three months a restore opens ten random photos; the decision is on the ticket.

## Unlocks
sub.19 (Kirsty's phone); sub.20 (photos are a family service); a later wider-family ticket if photos take off.

## Depends on
sub.11 (backups first). MYC-200 (Cloudflare R2 for Mycelium's family photos) is separate and only related.

- Finding 45: Nothing deleted from iCloud or staging (MCU-6) until the three-month decision.

intro.answer: Immich with phone upload, three months beside iCloud, then a restore and a decision.
intro.time: About 45 minutes over three sittings, three months apart at the end

hard_part.why: A restore needs both the files and the database dump.

steps.title: Install Immich
steps.body_html: Claude Code adds Immich to the config repo, puts its library on the data drive, and adds its upload folder and database dump to sub.11's backups.

steps.title: Create the admin and two users
steps.body_html: Create the admin account, then a user for you and one for Kirsty. Save each login in Proton Pass.

notes.html: Save the password in Proton Pass only. Never paste it into a chat, a ticket or the config repo.

steps.title: Install and sign in
steps.body_html: Install Immich, sign in to your user at the sporebit.com name, choose the albums to back up. Leave iCloud Photos as it is.

steps.title: First upload in the foreground
steps.body_html: Start the backup and keep the app open on charge and Wi-Fi until it finishes or for an evening. iOS does not promise background uploads.
steps.expect_html: Your photos appear on the web page.

phases.title: After three months: restore and decide

steps.title: Restore to a spare place
steps.body_html: Claude Code restores the upload folder and the database dump from the backup to a spare place and starts a second Immich on it.
steps.expect_html: The restored library opens with your photos and albums.

steps.title: Check the restore
steps.body_html: Open ten random photos, including recent ones and a video.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body_html: Decide: keep Immich beside the phones' cloud, rely on it more, or stop it.

fields.label: Decision after three months
fields.placeholder: keep beside, rely on it, or stop

tickets.title: Service: files and sync; phone and computer backups
tickets.description:
## What
Choose and run the files service on Substrate (Syncthing, Nextcloud, or both), sync the folders Phil lists between the PC, laptop and Substrate, give the phones access over the VPN, and settle what "phone backup" means: photos through Immich, files through this tool, full device backups where they already are unless a copied PC backup is chosen (check first).

## Why
Phil: personal data includes "files and sync" and "backups of phones and computers".

## Done looks like
A file made on the PC appears on the laptop and opens on the phone; the folders and the phone-backup line are written on the ticket; the data is in the nightly backup.

## Unlocks
sub.14, sub.15 (they use the same data drive and backups); sub.19 if Kirsty uses it.

## Depends on
sub.11 (backups first).

intro.answer: Choose the tool, sync the computers, reach files from the phone, settle phone backups.

steps.title: Choose
steps.body_html: Choose: Syncthing between PC, laptop and Substrate with phones reaching files over the VPN; or Nextcloud with its phone app; or both. Syncthing has no official iPhone app.

steps.title: List the folders
steps.body_html: Write which folders sync and which are only backed up.

steps.title: Set up on Substrate
steps.body_html: Claude Code adds the chosen tool to the config repo, with its data in sub.11's backups.
steps.expect_html: The tool answers at its sporebit.com name.

steps.title: Connect the PC and laptop

where.label: The tool's app on each computer

steps.body_html: Install the app, sign in or pair, and add the folders from step 1.2.
steps.expect_html: A test file made on the PC appears on the laptop.

steps.title: Phone access
steps.body_html: Install the chosen app, or add the Files app connection Claude Code gives, over the VPN.
steps.expect_html: You can open a PC file on the phone.

steps.title: Decide the phone backup line
steps.body_html: Photos go through Immich and files through this tool. A full iPhone device backup cannot go straight to a Linux server (check first); it stays in iCloud or in a PC backup copied to Substrate. Write which.

fields.label: Full phone backup
fields.placeholder: iCloud, or PC backup copied to Substrate

tickets.title: The Mycelium PC worker and FixForward's jobs on Substrate: power cost against benefit (RTX 4070 stays on the PC or a spare GPU)
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code writes a short costed comparison in Docs: (a) move the Mycelium PC worker's queue and FixForward's background jobs to Substrate and leave AI work on the main PC's RTX 4070 (the PC then wakes or stays on for AI only), against (b) a spare GPU in Substrate. Each line gives the extra watts (about 24p per watt per month), noise, what breaks when the PC is off, and the work to move. Phil picks one on the ticket; no move happens in this ticket.

## Why
Phil: AI if the worker moves, "research power cost against benefit" (queue on the server with AI left on the PC's RTX 4070, versus a spare GPU in the server).

## Done looks like
The Docs comparison exists with monthly figures, and Phil's choice is on the ticket.

## Unlocks
A later move ticket in E.brain or MYC once Phil chooses.

## Depends on
sub.16 (git and runners on Substrate); sub.01 (the measured idle figure).

## Cost
A spare GPU, if chosen, is to be priced. Nothing is bought in this run.

tickets.title: Each house service: a "what happens when it is off" test; internet and light switches work with the server off
tickets.description:
## What
With Substrate shut down in a weekend daytime slot, check the internet, light switches, heating and doorbell all still work; then start it and confirm every service returns by itself. Anything that does not work becomes a fix on the service's ticket before the 30-day proof.

## Why
Phil: "house basics fail safe: internet and light switches work with the server off; each house service gets a 'what happens when it is off' test".

## Done looks like
Every item ticked with the server off, and every service green again five minutes after starting.

## Unlocks
sub.25 (the 30-day proof only starts after this passes).

## Depends on
sub.08 (Home Assistant and the must-work list).

tickets.title: Each family service: "set up on Kirsty's phone", not done until untouched for a week
tickets.description:
## What
Set each family service up on Kirsty's phone with her, then leave it a week. A service is not done until it has worked on her phone for a week with nobody touching it. If anything needed touching, it goes back to its service ticket and the week restarts.

## Why
Phil: "invisible to her; each family service has a 'set up on Kirsty's phone' ticket and is not done until it works there untouched for a week".

## Done looks like
Every family service is listed as set up on Kirsty's phone, and a week later the untouched answer is yes.

## Unlocks
sub.25 and sub.26 (the proof and the done check).

## Depends on
sub.07 (the VPN on her phone first); sub.12 when photos are ready.

intro.answer: Set up with Kirsty, then a week untouched.

tickets.title: Family group of services: one set window, snapshot, rehearsed one-step revert, never on a weeknight
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code marks the family group in the config repo (the VPN, DNS filter, photos, Home Assistant, media and anything else Kirsty uses), sets one change window (a weekend daytime slot Phil names, in the monthly review only), and writes the one-step revert for each (snapshot taken first, revert to it in one command or one click), then rehearses one revert on photos and records how long it took. Each family runbook in Docs gains a "revert" line.

## Why
Phil, 7b: "no change without a tested way back and never on a weeknight (one set window, snapshot, rehearsed one-step revert); and a separate 'family' group of services touched only in the monthly review".

## Done looks like
The family group is listed; the window is on the ticket; one revert was rehearsed and timed; every family runbook has its revert line.

## Unlocks
sub.22 (monthly updates follow this rule); sub.25.

## Depends on
sub.12 (photos, the first family service the rehearsal uses); sub.02 (how snapshots work on the chosen platform).

tickets.title: Monitoring: a push through Mycelium and a status page
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code wires Uptime Kuma's alerts to a push through Mycelium (a webhook into a Mycelium endpoint that raises a notification, reusing the alerts address for backup and server reports where E.mail set it up), and publishes one status page reachable only at home or over the VPN. Backup job results from sub.11 report through the same route. No Mycelium endpoint is opened to Substrate from outside; Substrate calls out.

## Why
Phil: monitoring "both: a push through Mycelium and a status page".

## Done looks like
Stopping a test service sends a push to Phil's phone through Mycelium within a few minutes; the status page shows every service; a backup result arrives each night.

## Unlocks
sub.25 (the proof is read from the status page history).

## Depends on
sub.09 (the checks).

Every month, inside the monthly review, snapshot Substrate, update the non-family services and the host, then update the family services only in the set weekend window with the revert ready. The April 2027 review only reads the status page, because the 30-day proof runs from 2027-04-24 to 2027-05-24.

## Why
Phil: updates "in the monthly review, snapshot first".

## Done looks like
Each month: snapshots dated, every service green, any revert noted.

## Unlocks
Steady running for sub.25 and sub.26.

## Depends on
sub.04 (the config repo). It sits beside E.net's monthly review (net.24).

tickets.title: Restore test per service at set-up; a yearly timed rebuild drill on a spare drive
tickets.description:
## What
Each service gets one restore test when it is set up (its data restored from the backup to a spare place and checked), recorded in its runbook. Once a year, Substrate is rebuilt from scratch on a spare drive from the config repo and the backups, timed, and the gaps in the runbooks written down.

## Why
Phil, 7b rebuild promise, both: "a restore test per service at set-up, and a yearly timed rebuild drill on a spare drive".

## Done looks like
Every runbook shows a "restore tested" date; the yearly drill has a time in minutes and a gaps line.

## Unlocks
sub.26 (the done check trusts the backups because of this).

## Depends on
sub.11 (backups).

tickets.title: Printed "if it breaks" page for Kirsty

Phil, 7b bus test: "it needs nothing for a month, and there is a printed 'if it breaks' page for Kirsty".

## Done looks like
The page is by the routers and Kirsty has seen it.

## Unlocks
sub.25 (the proof assumes the page is there).

sub.07 (the VPN, so every service on the page exists).
